note: Layout Builder Reorder adds Move up / Move down links to each Layout Builder SECTION (core only reorders blocks within a section). It has no config, permission, service or drush. A #[Hook('element_info_alter')] adds SectionRearrangeRender::preRender as a #pre_render on the layout_builder element; that injects rearrange_up/rearrange_down AJAX links pointing at route layout_builder_reorder.move_section (/layout_builder/move/section/{section_storage_type}/{section_storage}/{delta}/{new_delta}); the MoveLayoutBuilderSectionController swaps the two sections' deltas in the Layout Builder tempstore and rebuilds via AJAX (access _layout_builder_access: view). Live cases use a namespaced content type lbr_reorder with Layout Builder overrides enabled: introspection reads the section order of a node's override layout; execution reorders the sections of a node's layout (the exact operation the module performs), verified by the resulting section order in layout_builder__layout.

evals.prompt: What does the layout_builder_reorder module add to Drupal's Layout Builder that core does not provide?
evals.expected_output: It adds Move up / Move down links to each Layout Builder section, letting you reorder whole sections. Core Layout Builder only lets you reorder blocks within a section, not the sections themselves.

evals.prompt: How does layout_builder_reorder add its Move up / Move down controls, and which route performs the actual section move? Does it define a new permission?
evals.expected_output: hook_element_info_alter adds SectionRearrangeRender::preRender as a #pre_render on the layout_builder element, which injects AJAX Move up/down links. They hit route layout_builder_reorder.move_section (/layout_builder/move/section/{section_storage_type}/{section_storage}/{delta}/{new_delta}), whose controller swaps the section deltas in the tempstore. It defines no new permission - access is _layout_builder_access: view.

evals.prompt: What configuration does layout_builder_reorder require after installing it, and does it add any settings form or Drush command?
evals.expected_output: None - it has no settings form (configure is null), no config, no permission, no service and no Drush command. Enabling the module is all that's required; the Move up/down links then appear wherever Layout Builder is used.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a node titled 'LBR Probe Node' whose Layout Builder override has two sections. Inspect its live layout and state the layout plugin id of the FIRST section.
evals.expected_output: The first section uses the layout_onecol layout (the node's layout_builder__layout sections are [layout_onecol, layout_twocol_section]).

evals.prompt: Inspect the Layout Builder override of the node titled 'LBR Probe Node' on this site and state how many sections its layout currently has.
evals.expected_output: It has 2 sections (layout_onecol followed by layout_twocol_section) in its layout_builder__layout field.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the node titled 'LBR Task Node' has a Layout Builder override with two sections, currently ordered one-column (layout_onecol) first and two-column (layout_twocol_section) second. Reorder the sections so the two-column section is first and the one-column section is second, then save the layout to the node.
evals.expected_output: The LBR Task Node's layout_builder__layout sections are reordered to [layout_twocol_section, layout_onecol] (the two-column section moved to the top) and saved.

evals.prompt: The node titled 'LBR Move Node' on this site has a Layout Builder override with three sections in order: one-column (layout_onecol), two-column (layout_twocol_section), three-column (layout_threecol_section). Move the one-column section to the bottom so it is the last section, keeping the other two in their relative order, and save the layout.
evals.expected_output: The LBR Move Node's layout_builder__layout sections end with layout_onecol last (e.g. order becomes [layout_twocol_section, layout_threecol_section, layout_onecol]), saved to the node.
